chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran who said:

I wrote to Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) or I said to him: May Allah make me your ransom - Do we worship The Beneficent, The Merciful, The Unique, The One, The Eternal? He said: He said: Indeed, whoever worships the name rather than the one named by the names has committed shirk, disbelieved, and denied, and has not worshipped anything. Rather, worship Allah the Unique, The One, The Eternal, who is called by these names and not the names themselves. Indeed, the names are attributes which He has described Himself with.

key_terms.الْمُسَمَّى: The Named One (the Essence being referred to by the name)

ai.seo_question: Do we worship the names of God or His Essence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) addresses the theological nuance between *al-Musamma* (the Named Essence) and *al-Isma* (the Name/Attribute), warning against idolizing the linguistic labels themselves. It establishes that divine names are merely attributes (*Sifat*) by which God described Himself, ensuring that worship remains directed solely at the transcendent Essence rather than the conceptual or verbal constructs. This distinction is crucial in Shia theology for maintaining pure monotheism (*Tawhid*) against forms of anthropomorphism or literalism.
